title: Why You Feel Hungry Even After Eating a Big Meal
hook: Why does a delicious smell make you hungry again?

narration.text: Your brain can make you feel hungry, even if your stomach is full.
Seeing or smelling food triggers a 'cephalic phase' response.
This prepares your body for digestion, releasing saliva and stomach acids.
It is an ancient reflex, designed to maximise nutrient absorption.
This response can trick your mind into thinking you need more food.
It is why you might crave dessert, even after a large dinner.
Do you find this happens to you often?

description:
Ever wondered why you feel hungry again just by seeing or smelling food, even after you have eaten? It is not just in your head. Your body has a fascinating ancient reflex that kicks in. 
Learn about the 'cephalic phase' response and how it influences your appetite, making you crave more.
topic: Why you might feel hungrier when you see or smell food, even if you just ate.
